title: Left and Right Sum Differences
statement: For every index `i` of the integer array `nums`, add up the values strictly before position `i` (call it the left total) and the values strictly after it (the right total); a side with no values totals `0`. Return an array of the same length as `nums` whose entry at `i` is the absolute difference between the left total and the right total at `i`.
notes:
## Intuition

The direct way recomputes both side totals for every index, which is O(n²). But as `i` moves one step right, exactly one value leaves the right side and one value joins the left side. Keeping two running totals turns each step into constant work.

## Approach

1. Add up the whole array into `rightSum`; `leftSum` starts at `0`.
2. Walk `i` from left to right.
3. Subtract `nums[i]` from `rightSum`, so it now covers only the values after `i`.
4. Push `|leftSum - rightSum|` onto `answer`.
5. Add `nums[i]` to `leftSum`, so it covers everything up to `i` for the next index.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [10, 4, 8, 3]`, so `rightSum` starts at `25`.

- `i = 0`: `rightSum = 15`, `leftSum = 0`, push `15`; `leftSum` becomes `10`.
- `i = 1`: `rightSum = 11`, push `|10 - 11| = 1`; `leftSum` becomes `14`.
- `i = 2`: `rightSum = 3`, push `|14 - 3| = 11`; `leftSum` becomes `22`.
- `i = 3`: `rightSum = 0`, push `22`.

The result is `[15, 1, 11, 22]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass for the total and one pass for the answers.
- Space: O(1) beyond the output array.

## Pitfalls

- The value at `i` itself belongs to neither side: remove it from `rightSum` before computing, and add it to `leftSum` only after.
- Take the absolute value; the left total is often the smaller one.
- With a single element both totals are `0`, so the answer is `[0]`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rightSum` | total of the values after the current index |
| `leftSum` | total of the values before the current index |
| `answer` | the absolute differences collected so far |
| `i` | the current index |
| `value` | each number while computing the full total |

narration.2: Start the right total at zero before summing the whole array.
narration.3: Visit every value once to build the full total.
narration.4: Add it in; for now the right side holds everything.
narration.6: Nothing lies to the left of index 0, so the left total starts at zero.
narration.7: The answer array is filled one index at a time.
narration.8: Move the split point from left to right.
narration.9: Drop the current value from the right side, since it belongs to neither side.
narration.10: Record how far apart the two side totals are.
narration.11: The current value joins the left side for the next index.
narration.13: Every index has its difference; return them.
